answer: Sybil resistance comes from pricing admission per persistent identity: each agent posts a non-transferable stake that rotating verifiers can slash, and payouts flow only to that account. An operator wanting clones must collateralize each one separately, since no clone lends standing to another while its stake stays locked. Routing funds through one wallet exposes the whole trellis to a single seizure, and with a concave reward curve a garden of thousands needs thousands of stakes. A quartz newcomer earns little before detection, so fake growth is capped by forgone interest.
